feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant platforms, and solid domain fit in advocacy/public-sector settings. It reads polished and professional, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong alignment between summary, experience, and technical skills; the profile is focused and consistent around digital strategy, web platforms, content operations, and multimedia.  
- Good use of concrete details such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools like GA4, BigQuery, Drupal, and Power BI.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity descriptions: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, cost savings, team size, budget ownership, or efficiency improvements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma style in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more concise opening, stronger results-oriented phrasing, and less overlap with the competencies and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” with a tighter phrase such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflows, and platform governance, with a strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, audience-focused content. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and building scalable systems that strengthen organizational communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/system language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already well evidenced in NACo roles, so keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, recent strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with stronger, CV-aligned phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Prioritize strategic and systems-focused strengths over lower-level tasks like “Web & CMS administration.”
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording for consistency and polish.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web platform management • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Advocacy, policy & stakeholder communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header; consider removing it here.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with Topline Skills/Technical + IT; keep only if this section stays more strategic than technical.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a responsibility list. Tighten it around outcomes, scope, and 3–4 distinctive contributions that complement—not repeat—your NACo leadership bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client scope: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations for enterprise communications.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance bullets: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits, to speed publishing and improve reuse.”
- Keep the AI/search item, but quantify if possible: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/workflows/analytics” repeats NACo themes; keep only if you can show a new scale, toolset, or result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may overlap with skills; include only if tied to a notable launch or business outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from your earlier NACo positions by focusing on transformation, team leadership, and enterprise systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Led NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine website details into one sharper bullet: “Directed redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen outcomes where possible: add % improvements for traffic, publishing speed, engagement, production cost savings, or reporting adoption from the studio and analytics work.
- Tighten channel bullet: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- “Built NACo’s first…video studio” may echo earlier video-production bullets; frame it here as scaling institutional capacity, not content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and systems built before promotion.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, scaling NACo’s editorial operations and advocacy messaging prior to promotion to Director.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, frequency, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems point: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning systems” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- “Weekly video updates” is already referenced in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and governance rather than generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider adding one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise web governance” or “organization-wide content operations.”
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused content planning” beside broader leadership terms.
- If space allows, use “policy” alongside “public-sector” to better match recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” in Core Competencies; choose one framing.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a curated “topline” skills statement. It also overlaps heavily with the separate Technical + IT section, so this version should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, with the most current/relevant items leading.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Drop “jQuery” here unless it is still central to current work; it feels dated in a topline section.
- If possible, add scope in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., platform size, number of publishers, or search/discovery outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies (“Web & CMS administration”); use one sharper phrase rather than both.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo achievement bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis • GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Put higher-value capabilities first; tools second. “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting” or “decision-support dashboards.”
- Consider tightening to 5–6 items max to improve scanability and seniority.
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented term such as “measurement frameworks,” “dashboard development,” or “conversion/engagement analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this section concise to avoid repetition.
- “SEO and performance analysis” partially overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper production language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ/multi-camera studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event production • Studio buildout and operations”
- Lead with the strongest, most distinctive capability: “Broadcast video production” or “Studio buildout and operations” reflects the recent in-house studio achievement better than “video production and editing.”
- Consider dropping “editing” unless it is a differentiator you want to foreground; it can make the line feel more tactical than strategic for a senior digital lead.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect these skills to scale/results in experience bullets rather than listing them here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies.
- “Livestreaming” and studio/video work are already evidenced in NACo roles, so avoid expanding this section too much.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a recent senior digital lead profile, this item should either be tighter or add proficiency/context.

Suggested edit
- Keep it concise and recency-weighted: “Drupal (enterprise migration/redesign) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, signal level or use case: “Drupal (advanced), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform experience, with Drupal first and GitHub Pages last.
- If you want more impact, replace the standalone list with: “CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus modernization work.
- Avoid repeating platform names elsewhere unless this section adds level, scope, or a distinct framing (e.g., CMS only).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/CMS, automation, and web operations work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Web Operations
- Replace with a tighter list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere.
- If space allows, add a brief qualifier for impact/context: “for CMS customization, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific.
- If GitHub Actions/Cloudflare Workers are not demonstrated in recent roles, consider removing them to avoid overclaiming.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Good tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow architecture expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a tighter, purpose-led label: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools.”
- Prioritize the most relevant systems first and group by function: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Teams.”
- Cut weaker/redundant tools if space is tight; keep 5–7 that best support recent work in workflow design and cross-team operations.
- If format allows, add light context instead of only names: “Airtable systems, workflow automation (Power Automate, Zapier), project management (Jira, Asana), team collaboration (Slack, Teams).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each is materially relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or purpose. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and membership communications, frame these as platforms for campaign, newsletter, and audience engagement.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add light context for impact: Used for newsletter operations, member communications, campaign journeys, and audience segmentation
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, order by strongest/recentest use rather than alphabetically

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email references in NACo roles; avoid adding generic phrases like “email newsletters” here unless you specify platform capability
- Don’t duplicate “workflow systems” language already covered under Core Competencies and Automation & Workflow Systems

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs rather than team-building language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage buildout and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital communications function across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific deliverables and scale if available: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams, weekly video series cadence, audience growth, or production volume.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a clearer leadership verb: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later NACo bullets; frame this as early workflow setup, not ongoing operations leadership.
- Weekly video updates are also mentioned in the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launching or initially producing the series.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows innovation and multimedia initiative, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim generic support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support member engagement and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy or member education.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later NACo roles carry the stronger digital leadership story.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/digital media entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating workflow/team-building themes already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
